extracted.intended_audience: members of the District of Columbia Bar, litigants and counsel appealing to the D.C. Court of Appeals, court clerks, and court reporters
extracted.subtask_short: D.C. appeals record and Bar governance rules
extracted.subtask_description: Official D.C. Court of Appeals and District of Columbia Bar governance rules describing board composition and duties, Executive Committee powers, meeting/ referendum procedures, financial/disbursement requirements, and detailed appellate record, transcript, waiver, transmission, and appendix requirements for appeals.

rubrics_metrics.name: President-elect succession and temporary service
rubrics_metrics.description: In the event of the death, permanent disability, or resignation of the President elect prior to January 1st, a special election shall be held to fill the vacancy. Until the election process is completed, the Board may elect one of its members to serve temporarily as Vice president.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies trigger events (death, permanent disability, resignation before Jan 1) and temporary leadership arrangement (Board may elect a member to serve as Vice President) pending a special election.

rubrics_metrics.name: Delegation of Secretary/Treasurer duties
rubrics_metrics.description: Any duties imposed by these Rules or by the By laws of the Bar upon the Secretary or Treasurer may be performed under the supervision of such officers, respectively, by assistants or by employees of the Bar.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allows delegation of administrative duties to assistants or employees, but performance remains under the supervising officer's oversight.

rubrics_metrics.name: Composition of Board of Governors
rubrics_metrics.description: The affairs of the Bar shall be managed and directed by a Board of Governors consisting of the officers of the Bar and the immediate past president of the Bar, who shall be ex officio members of the Board, and fifteen members elected by the members of the Bar in the manner prescribed by the By laws.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defines membership: officers + immediate past-president (ex officio) + fifteen elected members; election manner governed by Bylaws.

rubrics_metrics.name: Terms, qualifications, nomination, and election of Board members
rubrics_metrics.description: Treasurer-Elect shall be among the fifteen elected, non-officer members of the Board of Governors; at-large members shall be elected for terms (staggered one-, two-, three-year allocations described); Board members continue to serve until successors are elected and qualified; no person eligible to serve unless active member of the Bar; no person shall be eligible to election to the Board of Governors for more than 2 consecutive 3 year terms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies staggered terms for continuity, eligibility requirement (active membership), holdover until successor qualifies, and term limits (no more than two consecutive 3-year terms).

rubrics_metrics.name: Functions and authority of the Board of Governors
rubrics_metrics.description: The Board of Governors shall have general charge of the affairs and activities of the Bar in accordance with these Rules and the Bylaws. It shall have authority to fix the time and place of the annual meeting; to make appropriations and authorize disbursements; to engage and define duties of employees and fix compensation; to receive, consider and take action on reports and recommendations; to arrange for publication of an official Bar bulletin or journal; to conduct investigations of matters affecting the Bar; to fill vacancies in membership or offices; and to adopt Bylaws and regulations not inconsistent with these rules for orderly administration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enumerates core governance powers and administrative duties of the Board; includes filling vacancies and publishing official communications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Executive Committee composition
rubrics_metrics.description: There shall be an Executive Committee consisting of the President, the President elect, the immediate past president and 4 additional members selected annually by the Board of Governors from among their number.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defines size and selection method (board selects 4 additional members annually).

rubrics_metrics.name: Executive Committee chair and minutes
rubrics_metrics.description: The President shall preside at meetings of the Executive Committee and the Secretary shall keep minutes of its proceedings. The minutes of each meeting of the Executive Committee shall be immediately distributed to the members of the Board of Governors following such meeting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Designates presiding officer (President), minute-keeper (Secretary), and requirement for prompt distribution of minutes to full Board.

rubrics_metrics.name: Executive Committee powers and limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: The Executive Committee may exercise all the powers and perform all the duties of the Board of Governors between the meetings of the Board, except the Executive Committee shall not, unless otherwise authorized by the Board of Governors, (a) amend the By laws, (b) make rules for regulations governing nominations or elections, or (c) initiate the taking of any referendum or poll of members of the Bar.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Grants broad interim authority but explicitly lists three limitations requiring Board authorization (Bylaws amendment, nominations/election rules, initiating referenda/polls).

rubrics_metrics.name: Public expressions of Bar policy
rubrics_metrics.description: No opinion of the Bar on any matter involving legislation of major public interest or concern or of major importance to the members of the Bar shall be publicly expressed unless authorized by the Board of Governors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requires Board authorization before public statements on major legislative or membership-important matters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Executive Committee meeting procedures and quorum
rubrics_metrics.description: The Executive Committee shall meet at the call of the President, or upon call of the Secretary upon written application of 3 members upon 24 hours' notice. Five members shall constitute a quorum. Action of a majority of the members present at a meeting shall constitute action by the Committee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies how meetings are called, notice requirement, quorum number, and voting threshold (majority of those present).

rubrics_metrics.name: Annual meeting timing and content
rubrics_metrics.description: There shall be an annual meeting of members of the Bar during the month of June in each year. The Board of Governors shall determine the time and place and arrange a suitable program. Reports of officers and reports of proceedings of the Board of Governors subsequent to the last previous annual meeting shall be presented to the meeting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sets month for annual meeting, Board's role in arrangements, and required presentation of officers' and Board reports.

rubrics_metrics.name: Calling special meetings (members petition)
rubrics_metrics.description: Special meetings of the members of the Bar may shall be called by the Board of Governors or the President; and shall be called by the Secretary whenever he or she receives a petition signed by not less than 3% of the active members of the Bar requesting such meeting and specifying the purpose thereof, and the meeting shall be convened accordingly as promptly as possible and not later than 30 days after the Secretary receives such petition. The census of the Bar shall be determined as of the first business day of the calendar year in which the petition is submitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides members with a petition mechanism (3% threshold), timing (convene within 30 days), and census date for computing petition threshold.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quorum for member meetings and virtual attendance
rubrics_metrics.description: One hundred active members present at any annual or special meeting shall constitute a quorum. No member shall be entitled to be represented by proxy. For purposes of this Rule, 'present' shall include in person attendance, virtual/electronic attendance, or a combination thereof so long as all attendees can hear each other and participate meaningfully during such meeting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defines numeric quorum, prohibits proxies, and explicitly allows virtual participation if meaningful interaction is possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice requirements for meetings
rubrics_metrics.description: Notice of the time and place of every annual meeting shall be mailed by the Secretary to each active member or published in the official bulletin at least 30 days prior. Notice of the time, place and purpose of every special meeting shall be mailed or published at least 10 days prior to the meeting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sets distinct advance-notice periods for annual (30 days) vs. special meetings (10 days) and acceptable notice methods (mail or official bulletin).

rubrics_metrics.name: Assembly recommendations to Board of Governors
rubrics_metrics.description: The members present at any annual or special meeting may consider and by vote of the active members present adopt, subject to any limitations contained in the By laws, any proposal pertinent to the purposes of the Bar; provided that every such proposal that is adopted shall constitute a recommendation from the assembly to the Board of Governors, and shall be referred accordingly by the presiding officer to the Board for such action as the Board may deem proper, except as otherwise required in the case of a direction for a referendum under Rule VII, or in the case of a proposal for amendment of these rules under Rule XIV.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adopted proposals are recommendations to the Board and must be referred, with specified exceptions (referendum directions or rule amendments).

rubrics_metrics.name: Referendum initiation by Board
rubrics_metrics.description: The Board of Governors may at any time, by the affirmative vote of two-thirds of the Board, refer to the active members of the Bar for determination by mail member ballot, any question of Bar policy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allows Board-initiated mail ballots on policy with a two-thirds Board vote requirement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Referendum initiation by assembly (members at meetings)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Board shall submit for determination by the active members any question of Bar policy whenever directed to do so by resolution adopted at any annual or special meeting of the Bar by the affirmative vote of not less than 200 active members, provided that no such resolution directing the Board to propose changes in the rules shall be effective unless adopted at 2 consecutive meetings of the assembly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides an assembly-initiated path with a 200-member threshold, and for rule changes requires adoption at two consecutive meetings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Referendum initiation by petition of members
rubrics_metrics.description: The Board shall submit for determination by the members any question of Bar policy whenever directed so to do by a petition signed by not less than 3% of the active members of the Bar, based on the census as of the first business day of the calendar year in which the petition is submitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Member petition path with 3% threshold and specified census date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Referendum ballot procedure and effect
rubrics_metrics.description: Ballots for use in any such referendum shall be prepared, distributed, returned, and counted in accordance with regulations prescribed by the Board of Governors. The result of a referendum, as determined by a majority of the votes cast, when duly ascertained shall be published by the Board of Governors in the official Bar publication, and shall control the action of the Bar, the Board of Governors, the officers, and committees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedure delegated to Board regulations; majority of votes cast controls and result must be published.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disbursements, accounting, and audit requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: The Board of Governors shall make necessary appropriations for disbursements from the funds in the treasury to pay all necessary expenses of the Bar, its officers, employees, and committees. It shall be the duty of the Board to cause proper books of account to be kept and to procure an annual audit thereof by a certified public accountant. At each annual meeting the Board shall present a financial statement showing assets, liabilities, receipts, and disbursements. A copy shall be filed promptly with/transmitted to the Clerk of the District of Columbia Court of Appeals and published in an official publication prior to the annual meeting. The copy filed with/transmitted to the Clerk shall be accompanied by a detailed statement reflecting all significant components of the Bar's total disbursements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mandates bookkeeping, annual CPA audit, presentation and timely transmission/publication of detailed financial statements to the Court and membership.

rubrics_metrics.name: Promulgation of Bylaws
rubrics_metrics.description: Bylaws not inconsistent with these Rules may be promulgated/established by a majority vote of the voting members of the Board of Governors at a meeting with at least two-thirds of the voting Board members in attendance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sets voting and attendance (quorum) thresholds for adopting Bylaws: majority vote but requires presence of two-thirds of voting Board members.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendment of Rules (presentation to Court)
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposals for amendment of these Rules may be presented to the Court by (a) petition of the Board of Governors; or (b) petition of the assembly in respect of changes approved by referendum as provided in Rule VII. Hearing upon such a petition will be pursuant to notice in such manner as the Court may direct.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describes who may petition the Court to amend rules (Board or assembly via referendum) and that the Court will direct hearing notice procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendment of Bylaws (Board resolution threshold)
rubrics_metrics.description: The provisions of the By laws of the District of Columbia Bar shall be subject to amendment or abrogation by a resolution adopted by a majority vote of the voting members of the Board of Governors at a meeting with at least two thirds of the voting members of the Board members in attendance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Repeats the requirement for a majority vote plus two-thirds attendance to amend Bylaws.

rubrics_metrics.name: Record on Appeal composition
rubrics_metrics.description: The following items constitute the record on appeal: (1) the original papers and exhibits filed in the Superior Court; (2) the transcript of proceedings, if any; and (3) a certified copy of the docket entries prepared by the Clerk of the Superior Court.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defines the mandatory components that make up the record forwarded to the Court of Appeals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appellant's duty to order transcript (Rule 10(b)(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: Within 10 days after filing the notice of appeal, the appellant, unless proceeding on appeal as specified in Rule 10(b)(5), must: (A) order from the reporter a transcript of such parts of the proceedings not already on file as the appellant considers necessary, and identify for the Court Reporter Division any transcript already prepared that is to be included in the record on appeal; or (B) file a certificate in this court stating that no transcript will be ordered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ten-day deadline to order required transcript parts or file a certificate that none will be ordered; applies except where specified exceptions apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transcript requirement when challenging unsupported findings (Rule 10(b)(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: If the appellant intends to urge on appeal that a finding or conclusion is unsupported by the evidence or is contrary to the evidence, the appellant must include in the record a transcript of all evidence relevant to that finding or conclusion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When attacking factual findings, include complete transcript of all evidence relevant to the challenged finding (case law reference provided).

rubrics_metrics.name: Partial transcript procedures and designation timelines (Rule 10(b)(3))
rubrics_metrics.description: Unless the entire transcript is ordered: (A) the appellant must, within the 10 days provided in Rule 10(b)(1), file a statement of the issues the appellant intends to present and serve copies of transcript order/certificate and the statement; (B) other parties may, within 10 days after service, file and serve a designation of additional parts to be ordered; (C) unless the appellant orders all such parts within 10 days after service of that designation and notifies the parties, the designating party may within the following 10 days either order the parts or move in the Superior Court for an order requiring the appellant to do so.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establishes a timeline and procedure for incremental ordering of transcript parts and rights of other parties to designate and obtain additional parts or seek an order compelling the appellant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Payment arrangements for transcripts (Rule 10(b)(4))
rubrics_metrics.description: At the time of ordering, a party must make satisfactory arrangements with the Court Reporter Division for paying the cost of the transcript, except when the party is proceeding under Rule 10(b)(5).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requires payment arrangements upon ordering, with defined exceptions for certain indigent/appointed-counsel situations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transcript procedures in cases with fee waivers or appointed counsel (Rule 10(b)(5))
rubrics_metrics.description: Special procedures apply where appellant has waiver of fees/costs/security under Rule 24, where appellant proceeded under the Criminal Justice Act, or under the Prevention of Child Abuse and Neglect Act. Civil in forma pauperis requests must be made on motion to the trial judge; CJA cases treated as government-ordered transcript at government expense; child abuse counsel must secure vouchers and submit for approval.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describes motions, who bears cost, and administrative steps for obtaining transcripts when fees are waived or counsel appointed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statement of the evidence when transcript unavailable (Rule 10(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: If the transcript of a hearing or trial is unavailable, the appellant may prepare a statement of the evidence or proceedings from the best available means, including the appellant's recollection. The statement must be served upon all other parties, who may serve objections or proposed amendments within ten days. The statement and any objections must be submitted to the trial judge for settlement and approval; as settled and approved it must be included by the Clerk in the record on appeal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides a remedy when transcripts are unavailable: prepare agreed/settled statement, allow objections, submit to trial judge for settlement before inclusion in record.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agreed statement as alternative record on appeal (Rule 10(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: In place of the record on appeal, the parties may prepare, sign, and submit to the trial judge a statement of the case showing how the issues presented by the appeal arose and were decided. The statement must set forth only facts essential to resolution of the issues. If accurate, and with any necessary additions by the trial judge, it must be approved and certified to this court as the record on appeal. A copy may be filed in place of the appendix required by Rule 30.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allows parties to substitute an agreed, concise statement of the case for the full record; trial judge must approve and certify it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correction or modification of the record (Rule 10(e))
rubrics_metrics.description: (1) Differences about whether the record truly discloses what occurred must be submitted to and settled by the Superior Court and the record conformed accordingly. (2) Omitted or misstated material may be corrected and a supplemental record certified and forwarded on stipulation of the parties or by the Superior Court before or after the record has been forwarded. (3) All other questions as to the form and content of the record must be presented to this court.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies procedures for resolving disputes about accuracy or completeness of the record and available corrective mechanisms (stipulation or Superior Court action).

rubrics_metrics.name: Appellant duties for transmission of the record (Rule 11(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: An appellant filing a notice of appeal must comply with Rule 10(b) and must do whatever else is necessary to enable the Clerk of the Superior Court to assemble and forward the record. If there are multiple appeals from a judgment or order, the Clerk must assemble a single record.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Places responsibility on appellant to facilitate assembly and forwarding of the record and mandates a single assembled record for multiple appeals from same judgment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporter duties for transcript preparation and filing (Rule 11(b)(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: (A) Upon receiving an order for a transcript, the reporter must enter at the bottom of the order the date of its receipt and the expected completion date and send a copy so endorsed to the Clerk of the Superior Court. (B) If the transcript cannot be completed within 60 days of receipt, the reporter may request additional time from this court; the Clerk must note action and notify parties. (C) When complete, the reporter must file it with the Director of the Court Reporter Division.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requires reporting of receipt and expected completion, 60-day expectation with extension process, and filing steps with Director when complete.

rubrics_metrics.name: Director of Court Reporter Division duties (Rule 11(b)(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: If all transcript ordered or designated for appeal has not been completed within the 60-day period, the Director must retain the partial transcript until transcription of all proceedings is completed. When completed, the transcript must be placed in chronological sequence, with pages properly renumbered, and filed with the Clerk of the Superior Court.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Director consolidates partial transcripts, ensures chronological ordering and renumbering, and files completed transcript with Clerk.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clerk of Superior Court duties for forwarding the record (Rule 11(b)(3))
rubrics_metrics.description: (A) When the record is complete, the Clerk must prepare an index that reasonably identifies and numbers the documents constituting the record, and promptly send 4 certified copies of that index and the original reporter’s transcript, if any, to the Clerk of this court. The Clerk must retain all other parts of the record for the parties to use, subject to call by this court. In waiver cases the Clerk must prepare and submit 2 copies of the record. (B) If reporter’s transcript is filed after transmittal of the certified index, the Clerk must forward the transcript as a supplemental record promptly after the Director files it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sets indexing and certified-copy transmittal obligations, retention of originals for parties, special reduced-copy rule for waiver cases, and supplemental transcript forwarding procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preliminary record transmission for motions (Rule 11(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: If, before the record is forwarded, a party files in this court a motion for dismissal, summary reversal/affirmance, release pending appeal, stay, injunction, additional security, or other relief, the Clerk of the Superior Court, upon order of this court, must transmit a preliminary record containing the notices of appeal, the order appealed from, and those parts of the record designated by any party.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allows the Court to obtain a preliminary record for resolution of certain urgent/preliminary motions before full record transmission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standards governing waiver of fees, costs, or security (Rule 24 general)
rubrics_metrics.description: The standards governing eligibility for waiver are listed in D.C. Code § 15-712(a).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Directs users to statutory standards for in forma pauperis eligibility; Rule 24 implements statutory framework for appeals and filings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeals from Superior Court — prior approval and filing for waiver (Rule 24(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: (1) A party granted a waiver in the Superior Court or determined eligible for court-appointed counsel under specified statutes may proceed on appeal without paying fees. (2) Except as stated in (1), a party seeking to appeal without paying must file in the Superior Court within the time for filing an appeal: (i) A notice of appeal containing information prescribed in Form 1 or Form 2; and (ii) An application to waive court fees, costs, or security pursuant to Superior Court Rule of Civil Procedure 54-II. If Superior Court grants the waiver, the party may proceed on appeal without paying. If denied, the party may request a hearing and thereafter may file in this court an application to proceed without paying, including Form 7 materials and additional evidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requires initial filing in Superior Court for waiver requests related to appeals and provides appeal/administrative steps if denied; includes required documentation and declaration (Form 7) for Court of Appeals applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Waiver applications filed directly in Court of Appeals (Rule 24(b)(3))
rubrics_metrics.description: If a party seeks to proceed on appeal without paying after having filed a notice of appeal and paid required fees, the party must file with this court an application to waive court costs, fees, or security (Form 7) and sign the declaration contained in Form 7.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Permits filing in this Court when fees already paid with required form and signed declaration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Waiver procedure for petitions for review and extraordinary writs (Rule 24(c),(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: When review of an agency decision proceeds directly to this court, or when filing petitions for extraordinary writs, a party may file with the petition an application to waive costs (Form 7) and sign the declaration; must be filed within the time permitted for seeking review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensures waiver application accompanies direct petitions and follows the petition timing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing for deciding waiver applications (Rule 24(e))
rubrics_metrics.description: (1) Within 5 calendar days after receiving a completed waiver application, the court must decide whether to approve. The Clerk, if authorized, may grant waivers. (2) If not ruled within 5 calendar days, the application is deemed approved. (3) Deadlines do not apply where the court requires additional information under D.C. Code § 15-712(b)(1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Creates expedited decision timeline (5 days) with automatic approval if court fails to act, subject to statutory exceptions for supplemental information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Denial of waiver applications and hearing rights (Rule 24(f))
rubrics_metrics.description: If a waiver application is denied by this court, the court shall state reasons in writing. A party denied in whole or in part may request a hearing under statute; a hearing must be held no later than 14 days after the court receives the hearing request. If after the hearing the waiver is denied, the party must pay the required filing fee within the time specified in the final order of denial.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guarantees written reasons, a prompt hearing schedule (14 days), and payment obligations upon final denial.

rubrics_metrics.name: Court must not consider merits when deciding waiver (Rule 24(g))
rubrics_metrics.description: In considering a waiver application, the court must not consider the merits of the appeal or petition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Separates financial eligibility determination from merits to avoid prejudging the appeal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Motions for free transcripts or other documents (Rule 24(h))
rubrics_metrics.description: (1) Civil cases: a party granted a waiver may file a motion in Superior Court requesting free transcripts or documents; the Superior Court must grant unless the request is frivolous, resolving doubt in favor of the applicant; the court may order only portions necessary to resolution. (2) Criminal cases: where appellant proceeded under the Criminal Justice Act, the notice is considered an order for preparation of transcript at government expense; in other criminal cases a defendant granted a waiver may file motion in Superior Court requesting free transcripts which will be considered as an order for preparation at government expense under procedures specified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describes strong presumption in favor of providing necessary transcripts to indigent parties in civil cases and mechanisms for government-funded transcripts in criminal/CJA contexts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidentiality of waiver applications (Rule 24(i))
rubrics_metrics.description: (1) The court must keep confidential an application and any financial information submitted, except to the court, the litigant, persons authorized by the litigant, or by court order. The application must not be served on the other party. (2) Motion for access: (A) Any person seeking access may file a motion with notice to the litigant supported by a declaration showing good cause. (B) Any person granted access shall not reveal information except as authorized by law or court order. (3) The court’s decision on an application for a waiver shall not be confidential.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Protects applicants' financial data, restricts disclosure, provides a good-cause access process, and clarifies that the court's decision is public.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special rules governing appeals without payment (Rule 24(j))
rubrics_metrics.description: For rules specially governing appeals proceeding without payment of fees, costs, or security, see Rules 10(b)(5), 11(b)(3), and 30(f).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cross-references other rules that contain special procedures for indigent appeals and appointed counsel situations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appendix contents for briefs (Rule 30(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: The appellant must prepare and file an appendix to the briefs containing: (A) the relevant docket entries in the proceeding below; (B) the relevant pleadings, charge, findings, or opinion; (C) the judgment, order, or decision in question; and (D) other parts of the record to which the parties wish to direct the court's attention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies mandatory and optional materials to include in the appendix that supports the appellate briefs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Excluded material from appendix (Rule 30(a)(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: Memoranda of law filed in the Superior Court should not be included in the appendix unless they have independent relevance. Parts of the record may be relied on by the court or the parties even though not included in the appendix.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discourages including unnecessary trial memoranda; reminds that appendix is a subset and the court can access the full record independently.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appendix filing copies and service (Rule 30(a)(3))
rubrics_metrics.description: The appellant must file 4 copies of the appendix with the brief and must serve one copy on counsel for each party separately represented.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies number of copies to file and service obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Parties' coordination on appendix contents and designations (Rule 30(b)(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: Parties are encouraged to agree on the contents of the appendix. In absence of agreement, the appellant must, within 20 days after the Clerk notifies the parties that the record is filed, serve on all other parties a designation of the parts intended for the appendix and a statement of the issues. Any other party may, within 10 days, serve a designation of additional parts to which it wishes to direct the court's attention. The appellant must include designated parts. Parties must not engage in unnecessary designation because the entire record is available to the court.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encourages cooperation, sets timelines for designation (20 days and 10 days), and discourages over-inclusion to avoid unnecessary burden.

rubrics_metrics.name: Costs and sanctions for appendix (Rule 30(b)(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: Unless parties agree otherwise, the appellant must pay the cost of the appendix. If the appellant considers parts designated by another party unnecessary, the appellant may advise that party, who must then advance the cost of including those parts. The cost of the appendix is a taxable cost. If any party causes unnecessary parts to be included, the court may impose the costs of those parts on that party and appropriate sanctions after notice and opportunity to respond.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allocates financial responsibility for appendix content, makes costs taxable, and authorizes sanctions for unreasonable increases in litigation costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Format requirements for the appendix (Rule 30(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: The appendix must begin with a table of contents identifying the page at which each part begins. Pages must be numbered consecutively. The relevant docket entries must follow the table of contents, and other parts must follow chronologically. When transcript pages are placed in the appendix, the date of each transcript and the page numbers must be listed on a separate page immediately before the included pages. Omissions in text must be indicated by asterisks. Immaterial formal matters (captions, subscriptions, acknowledgments, etc.) should be omitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies organization, pagination, transcript labeling, omission marking, and trimming of immaterial formalities for clarity and usability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reproduction and filing of exhibits in appendix (Rule 30(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: Exhibits designated may be reproduced in a separate volume(s), suitably indexed. Four copies must be filed with each copy of the appendix, and one copy must be served on counsel for each separately represented party. If a transcript of an administrative proceeding used in Superior Court action is designated, the transcript must be placed in the appendix as an exhibit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sets indexing, copy count, service obligations, and handling of agency transcripts used in underlying proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeal on original record without appendix (Rule 30(e))
rubrics_metrics.description: For good cause shown, the court may excuse a party from producing an appendix, or any part thereof, and permit an appeal to proceed on the original record with any copies of the record, or relevant parts, that the court may order the parties to file.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allows waiver of appendix requirement in exceptional circumstances; court may order alternative record copies as needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appendix requirements in appeals with fee waivers or appointed counsel (Rule 30(f))
rubrics_metrics.description: No appendix is required in cases in which a party has been granted a waiver of fees, costs, or security or counsel has been appointed to represent the party. In such cases, however: (1) The appellant must file with the brief 4 copies of any opinion, findings of fact, and conclusions of law, whether written or set forth orally in the transcript, that relate to the issues raised; and (B) may, but is not required to, file with the brief 4 copies of any additional portions of the record to be called to the court's attention. (2) The appellee may file with the brief 4 copies of any portions of the record to be called to the court's attention that were not furnished by the appellant. (3) A copy must be served on counsel for each party separately represented.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Creates simplified appendix obligations for indigent parties or appointed counsel: required filing of four copies of dispositive opinions/findings, optional additional records, and appellee rights to file missing parts.
